mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact corporate earnings and thus drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as investor confidence drops.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the unemployment rate is below 4%, it indicates a tight labor market and high interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting corporate profitability and leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If during a tightening cycle, S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as companies increase output and revenues.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1000 units indicates weak demand in the housing market, leading to negative economic growth and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts fall below 1000 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 45% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth is strong and federal funds rate increases, it may indicate inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as companies adapt to growth.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment rates signal a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as consumer spending remains robust.
failure_condition: If unemployment is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.
